newsitem.title: USA: Tyler, Texas, plans bond sale for water plant.
newsitem.headline: Tyler, Texas, plans bond sale for water plant.

text.p: Tyler, Texas, plans to sell up to $36 million of revenue bonds to help finance a $53 million water treatment plant expected to be on line by 2001 or 2002, a city official said.
The bonds most likely would be sold around 1999, Ed Ilschner, Tyler's assistant city manager for utilities and public works, said.

"We getting to where we are approaching our capacity in the current water supply by the year 2000, 2001," Ilschner said. "And when this plan comes on line it will give us an additional 15 million gallons per day, which will provide the additional water we need for growth."
First Southwest Co will probably underwrite the issue, he said.
"We have a relationship currently with First Southwest and unless the city changes its underwriter, First Southwest would probably be who we would work with on the issue," Ilschner said.

The city will provide the balance out of revenues set aside in a construction reserve fund. The city funds--expected to total roughly $17 million--will be used first, he said. Tyler is located in Northeast Texas, approximately 90 miles east of Dallas.
